change: Links to live work (play it, see it live, the source, press) moved from buttons under the colored band into one quiet line inside it. An arrow pointing up and out means the link leaves the site.

The colored title band now sits right under the back bar. Company and case study pages use one rhythm: a larger gap between blocks, a smaller one inside a group, no doubled-up gaps. The project cards got their section heading back.

HogWare, Zodiacus, and This site now use the same header as company pages and read like a case study: the "What I did" summary, one row of facts, the outcome, then credits. "Role details" is gone everywhere.

Took the fact band and "Role details" apart. The role and dates sit above the company name, the "What I did" summary introduces the projects, and credits (who worked on it, and who wrote the code) close the page. Case studies open with their summary and close with their own credits.
Removed the numbers from the "Also shipped" lists. They read like steps in a process, and the items aren't sequential.
Added this page, a living record of how the site is designed, and made the design system behind it public.

Every project card is now the same card, on company pages and the homepage. Hovering tilts it toward the cursor with a soft glow, and tall screenshots scroll. One or two cards stretch to fill the row.
Recent work now leads the homepage: three recent case studies, one click away.
Company pages became an index. A short fact band (when, what I owned, the outcome) comes first, then the projects. The full details fold away at the bottom.
Each company keeps its own color, but only as a band behind its title. The rest of the page uses the site's own paper and type, so it reads as one site.
Set four speeds and three easing curves for all motion, based on published design systems.
Replaced about thirty different gaps with four: tight within a group, more between items, more between groups, most between sections.
Cut 26 text sizes down to one scale. Nothing on the site is smaller than 14 pixels.
Two typefaces, two weights, and square corners everywhere.
The homepage opens on one full-screen statement. The work starts one scroll below.
